title: Rice, white, long grain, unenriched, raw

content.title: About
content.content: White long‑grain rice is milled rice with the husk, bran, and germ removed. It has a mild flavor, fluffy texture when cooked, and is a staple in many world cuisines.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Long‑grain rice stays separate after cooking, making it ideal for pilafs and fried rice.
Removing the outer layers extends shelf life but reduces vitamins and minerals.
In Japan rice is a cultural symbol of prosperity and is featured in many traditional dishes.
More than half of the world’s population relies on rice as a primary food source.
There are over 40 000 rice varieties, but only a small fraction are long‑grain.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Rice is rich in carbohydrates that quickly convert to glucose, providing readily available energy.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: White rice has a soft texture and low fiber content, making it gentle on the digestive system.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Rice contains no gluten, suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: It provides modest amounts of thiamine, niacin, and vitamin B6, which support metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Rice supplies magnesium and phosphorus, important for bones and nerve function.

items.title: Low fiber content
items.content: White rice provides little dietary fiber, which can contribute to constipation if eaten in excess.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: It can cause rapid spikes in blood sugar, a concern for people with diabetes.

items.title: Arsenic
items.content: Rice may accumulate arsenic from soil in some regions; rinsing and cooking in excess water can reduce levels.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook rice in water or broth until tender. Use it in pilafs, sushi, soups, salads, or as a side dish for meat and fish. Rinse rice before cooking to remove excess starch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry rice in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For long‑term storage, keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent insect infestation.
